purpose: Authoritative-vendor manufacturing maintenance integration delta adding Fracttal One at spec-verified only. Reuses the existing REST/OpenAPI transport, records OAuth2 permission-group, pagination, rate-limit, custom-field, multi-site and write-authority boundaries, and keeps Manufacturing WFM read-only. No sandbox/customer credentials, customer data, writes or plant-network probes were used.

systems.name: Fracttal One
systems.evidenceNote: Current Fracttal documentation confirms a JSON REST API secured with OAuth 2.0. OAuth consumers support Client Credentials or Authorization Code and must be associated with a permission group that controls accessible resources and actions. Read endpoints cover assets/locations/equipment/tools/spares, work orders and tasks, pending tasks, work requests, meters/readings, personnel references, custom fields and work-order material movements. Most list endpoints use start/limit pagination with a default/maximum page size of 100; vendor FAQ documents a 200 requests/minute API limit, and dynamic filters are bounded. The same API also supports create/update/delete operations, including advanced work-order creation, so WFM requires a dedicated read-only permission group and never treats OAuth success alone as proof of least privilege. Public documentation still contains legacy Hawk-authentication material alongside the current OAuth2 contract; deployment/version discovery must therefore pin the actual supported auth/API contract before authentication evidence can advance. No Fracttal tenant was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated OAuth2 consumer, preferably Client Credentials, associated with a customer-created permission group containing only the minimum GET/read resources required for WFM
read assets/locations/equipment, work orders/tasks, pending tasks, work requests, meters/readings and inventory/material context only where the customer approves each domain
tenant/company and site/location hierarchy bound explicitly; do not accept a token whose effective permission group can create, update or delete maintenance, asset, inventory or personnel records
exclude personnel document bodies and unrelated personal data by default; use only the minimum worker/resource reference needed for assignment reconciliation
no advanced-API work-order creation, task update, stock mutation, personnel creation, configuration or administrative authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: asset hierarchy covering locations, equipment, tools, spares/supplies and customer custom fields
maintenance work orders and associated tasks, status, dates, responsible resource references and asset context
pending/planned maintenance tasks, work requests/incidents, urgency/status and request-to-work-order lifecycle context
meter definitions/readings and last-maintenance context where the customer's plan/add-on exposes them
work-order material requisitions, warehouses/spares context and inventory resources associated with maintenance tasks
human-resource/personnel identifiers and assignment references where required for deterministic WFM worker reconciliation
automationOpportunities: forecast technician/headcount demand from pending and planned maintenance before it becomes emergency overtime or agency labour
match WFM availability and verified qualifications to Fracttal work-order demand while keeping Fracttal personnel/resource data as assignment context rather than employment authority
avoid dispatching labour when required spare/material readiness is missing and surface the constraint before shift execution
use meter/asset condition and urgent work-request context to prioritize maintenance coverage and coordinate production downtime windows
reconcile maintenance labour demand, responsible-resource assignments and completion timing against WFM paid time for cost/downtime attribution

future controlled write candidate: create/update Fracttal work orders only after separate write-roundtrip, idempotency, approval and customer-authority evidence; disabled in the normal connector plane
savingsHypotheses: reduce emergency overtime and contractor/agency call-outs by forecasting maintenance labour and skill demand from pending work earlier
reduce maintenance-related production loss by aligning qualified labour and required material availability before the planned intervention window
reduce manual maintenance-to-timesheet reconciliation through deterministic work-order, asset, responsible-resource and timestamp joins
improve labour-to-asset/downtime cost attribution for maintenance, operations and finance without making Fracttal the payroll source
reduce bespoke CMMS integration effort by reusing the existing REST adapter, standard OAuth2 service identity and common offset-pagination controls
dataGaps: Fracttal is not normally authoritative for employment contracts, payable attendance, absence, payroll, agency commercials or complete workforce availability
personnel/resource records do not by themselves prove qualification, legal eligibility or current skill certification
exact enabled endpoints depend on customer plan/add-ons; advanced APIs and optional modules cannot be assumed present
customer custom fields, asset codes, location hierarchy and responsible-resource identifiers require versioned customer-specific canonical mappings
public documentation spans multiple generations/languages and includes older Hawk-authentication guidance, so the effective tenant API/auth version must be discovered rather than inferred
constraintsRisks: the REST surface is bidirectional; WFM must verify the OAuth permission group's effective operations are read-only instead of relying on GET-only client intent
most list endpoints cap pages at 100 records and use start/limit or page semantics; extraction must continue until completion and reconcile stable IDs across overlapping incremental windows
the documented 200 requests/minute limit requires per-tenant budgeting, bounded concurrency, Retry-After/backoff handling where returned, and no credential-sharding to evade throttling
dynamic filters are bounded and date/time values can include UTC offsets; filter encoding, timezone normalization and source timestamps must be preserved

partial add-on coverage, intermittent API availability, duplicate/changed records and schema/custom-field drift must fail to advisory/stale-data mode rather than silently producing complete-looking workforce decisions
write-capable advanced endpoints exist, including work-order creation; they remain outside the normal connector authority until separate controlled write evidence is earned
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI adapter and generic connection-evidence gate. In an authorised Fracttal sandbox/customer tenant, first discover the effective API/auth generation, create a dedicated OAuth2 Client Credentials consumer with a read-only permission group, prove tenant/company/site scope and actual permitted operations, then perform bounded GET reads for assets, work orders/tasks, pending tasks, work requests and meters. Validate 100-record pagination, the 200-requests/minute budget/backoff, date filters/timezones, custom-field schema fingerprints, stable-ID deduplication, partial/add-on behaviour and resource-to-WFM identity mappings before promotion beyond spec verification. Keep all POST/PUT/DELETE and Advanced API write paths disabled until a separately authorised write-roundtrip programme exists.
